title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-jordan-lee
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for GPU OOM + driver/library mismatch incidents observed on staging-GPU nodes. Mixing kernel logs, commands I ran, hypotheses and next steps. Mainly for me and Asha/Raja follow-up.

Summary of incident (2026-02-10 15:20 UTC):
- Inference r12 (long-context Llama variant) started failing on node gpu-stg-03 with OOMs during rolling canary.
- Symptoms: worker process crashed with CUDA OOM. Prior to crash, occasional "Driver/library version mismatch" messages in container logs.
- Repro: not deterministic — hits after ~20–200 queries depending on sequence length.

Commands / outputs I captured:
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee)

$ nvidia-smi
Tue Feb 10 15:05:02 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03   Driver Version: 535.54.03   CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
|        ID   ID                                                   Usage      |
|=============================================================================|
|    0   N/A  N/A      2140      C   python                           37542MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Note: host driver 535, reports CUDA 12.1.

2) Container/containerized runtime errors (from pod logs)\Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/run_inference.py", line 412, in <module>
    out = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=1024)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in __call__
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in __call__
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.50 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 37.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 35.62 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

Before some crashes we also saw: 
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxxx] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_IN_DRIVER (known message in other contexts)
W tensorflow/core/common_runtime/gpu/gpu_device.cc:xxx] Cannot dlopen some GPU libraries: libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

And intermittently in logs: "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"

3) dmesg / kernel messages around failure\$ dmesg | tail -n 40
[ 43212.345678] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:00:1e.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 43212.345689] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e.0): 32, Ch 00000002, GPU has fallen off the bus

Interpretation: that Xid 32 (GPU fell off the bus) often correlates with driver mismatch/memory ECC errors or occasionally with heavy OOM + GPU reset. Need to correlate with system logs.

What I tried (chronological):
- Repro locally in a dev container with smaller model and long context: yes reproduced OOM-ish behavior but no driver crash.
- Verified host driver: nvidia-smi on host OK (535).
- Entered container and checked cuda toolkit/pytorch versions:
  $ python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.__version__)"
  -> torch 2.2.0+cu117, torch.version.cuda = '11.7'
  Container compiled against CUDA 11.7 (cu117) but host driver advertises 12.1 -> generally compatible (newer drivers support older CUDA runtimes) but not guaranteed for certain lib version combos.
- ldd checks inside container: ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so -> shows link to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host provided)
- Checked libcudnn inside container: ls /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn* -> missing libcudnn.so.8; only libcudnn_adv_infer.so.8 exists (odd).
- Reinstalled cudnn in image (pip/apt mix) to try to match — caused more library mismatch errors. Rolled back.
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced and dockerd on host; recreated the pod -> sometimes clears the "Driver/library version mismatch" transiently.
- Reduced batch_size / reduce max_new_tokens during test -> reduces speed of hitting OOM; suggests memory pressure is main cause.
- Looked at our inference code: noticed we keep KV cache in memory across repeated incremental calls (we already have a cache eviction mechanism but may not be triggered for long contexts). Suspect KV cache leak or high retention for multi-turn tests.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: memory pressure (long sequences + large batch) causes PyTorch to fragment memory; after enough allocation/free cycles fragmentation + reserved caching leads to perceived OOM even when memory exists.Combined with driver/other lib mismatch, process-level reset (Xid 32) may occur.
2) Secondary: mismatch between container CUDA runtime (11.7) and host driver (12.1) plus missing/incorrect libcudnn in container causes some operations to fallback or trigger undefined behavior causing GPU to reset.
3) Tertiary: nvml/nvidia-container-toolkit versions inconsistent across nodes, leading to intermittent "Failed to initialize NVML" and odd visibility/metrics; not root cause of OOM but complicates debugging.

Quick reproducer to run: (minimal.py)
- create short script that allocates tensors repeatedly with model.generate-like pattern and long max_new_tokens until OOM. Add explicit torch.cuda.empty_cache() and monitor reserved vs allocated.
- record nvidia-smi -l 1 in separate terminal and dmesg -w to catch Xid if occurs.

Potential fixes to test (short-term):
- Force container to use torch+cu117 but install matching libcudnn8 packages from NVIDIA apt for cudnn compatible with host driver (install nvidia/cuda repo package that maps to driver 535).
- Pin driver on host to 535 (it's already 535) and ensure nvidia-container-toolkit >= 1.10 (check compat matrix).
- Enable TORCH_USE_RTLD_GLOBAL=1 when launching container (helps with some dlopen issues).
- Add process-level memory guard: limit max_new_tokens at serving layer + reduce default batch size + better per-request memory accounting (reject if predicted cost > X).
- Implement periodic model reload (as workaround) to clear fragmentation on long-running workers.

Longer-term / infra changes:
- Standardize a small matrix of approved (driver, nvidia-toolkit, cuda-runtime, libcudnn, torch) combos and bake them into our base runtime images.
- Add test harness that runs long-sequence multi-turn workloads on canary nodes to detect fragmentation/leaks before rollout.

Notes / breadcrumbs for next run:
- Check host /var/log/messages around 2026-02-10 15:05 for additional Xid codes (Xid 31 vs 32).
- Grab full ldd list for libtorch_cuda.so and libcudnn* from working and failing containers.
- Reproduce with latest torch build for cu121 (if available) in separate node that reports CUDA 12.x to see whether aligning runtime solves resets.
- Ask infra to temporarily cordon node gpu-stg-03 and run driver reinstall if Xid keeps happening.

Things I learned (for myself):
- "Driver/library version mismatch" often comes from container's CUDA toolkit headers/libraries not lining up with host libcuda (or mismatched libcudnn). Newer driver -> older toolkit sometimes works, but mixing apt/pip installs of cudnn can silently break.
- Xid 32 "GPU fell off the bus" is severe — treat as GPU reset and check for hardware faults if reproducible across drivers.

Action items (TODO):
- [ ] Create minimal repro script and run on gpu-stg-03 with live logging (Asha).
- [ ] Collect ldd outputs from failing container and a known-good node (Raja).
- [ ] Try container image with torch built for CUDA 12.1 on one canary node (me).
- [ ] Add heuristic in serving layer to cap max_new_tokens by tenant until we resolve fragmentation/risk (short-term mitigation).

References / snippets saved:
- Common error: "Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch" -> usually nvml-provided libcuda.so mismatch (search stack overflow threads).
- Xid docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/index.html

End of notes.

(If I don't come back to this: follow the TODOs above and ping infra channel with timestamps & dmesg outputs so ops can correlate with NVIDIA support if hardware suspected.)
